testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What is a Class 1 hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are explosives.

questions.question: When stopping your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Press the brake pedal down quickly.
Press the brake pedal down slowly and smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal down slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: Always press the brake pedal down slowly and smoothly when stopping.

questions.question: How can you prevent fatigue on long trips?
questions.explanation: To prevent fatigue on long trips, take a break every 100 miles or every 2 hours. Driving when you would normally be sleeping increases the risk of fatigue.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.

questions.explanation: Plan ahead with realistic travel times to reduce frustration that can lead to aggressive driving. Other tips include driving at a safe speed, keeping distance from other vehicles, avoiding rude gestures, and keeping both hands on the wheel.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of tie-down equipment?
questions.explanation: Proper tie-down equipment includes ropes, straps, and chains. Velcro is not used to secure cargo on a flatbed trailer.

questions.question: How can you prevent distracted driving?
questions.explanation: Distractions can be physical (reaching for objects), mental (conversations), or both (texting). To prevent distracted driving, pre-program your radio, plan your route, avoid complex conversations, adjust mirrors before driving, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: To transport hazardous materials, you must:
questions.explanation: You must have a hazardous materials endorsement to transport any hazardous materials that require vehicle placards.

questions.question: The ____ turn on when the brake pedal is pressed.
questions.explanation: Brake lights are activated by an electric switch triggered by the brake pedal. When you press the brake pedal, air pressure moves the switch to turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: If there is a vehicle fire and you are unsure how to put it out, you should:

options.text: Move away from the fire and wait for firefighters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move away from the fire and wait for firefighters.
questions.explanation: If you are unsure how to put out a fire, do not try to extinguish it yourself. Move away and wait for firefighters. This is especially important for hazardous materials fires.

questions.question: If a speed limit is posted, the posted speed:

options.text: May be exceeded when passing another vehicle.
May be exceeded in rural areas.

questions.explanation: Posted speed limits are the maximum speed allowed under ideal conditions. Always slow down based on road and weather conditions. Never exceed the posted speed limit.

questions.question: If you are driving in very hot weather and your tire air pressure is too high, what should you do?

options.text: Let air out of the tire.
Stop and let the tires cool down before driving again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the tires cool down before driving again.
questions.explanation: Hot air expands, so tire pressure gets higher in very hot weather. If your tire pressure is too high, stop and let the tires cool. Do not let air out. If you do, the pressure will drop too much when the tires cool down.

questions.question: What does a trailer brake hand valve do on a truck?

options.text: Keep the truck from rolling backward when you start from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the truck from rolling backward when you start from a stop.
questions.explanation: The trailer brake hand valve helps stop a tractor-trailer from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.question: After you secure cargo on a vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: You do not need to check the cargo again.
Do not let others inspect the cargo.

questions.explanation: Check your cargo before you start driving, within the first 50 miles, and then every 150 miles or every three hours after that.

questions.question: What color light shows that a vehicle's ABS is broken?
questions.explanation: On vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS), a yellow warning light tells the driver that the ABS is not working.

questions.question: When you load a trailer, where should you place the weight?

options.text: As far to the left as possible.

questions.explanation: Cargo that is high up makes a vehicle more likely to tip over. Cargo that is low is safer. Always place weight as low as possible.

questions.question: What happens if you exit your vehicle incorrectly during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: You get an extra point taken away from your score.
You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When you exit your vehicle during the test, you must face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. For a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly means you fail the whole test.

questions.question: In cold weather, when do bridges usually freeze?

options.text: After other parts of the road.
Before other parts of the road.
At the same time as other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces in cold weather. Be extra careful on bridges and overpasses when it is cold and wet.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher, what should you do?

options.text: Get as close to the fire as possible.
Stay as far from the fire as possible.
Aim at the top of the fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay as far from the fire as possible.
questions.explanation: Stay as far from the fire as possible. Aim at the base of the fire, not the flames. If you are not sure which extinguisher to use, especially for hazardous materials, wait for firefighters.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, what should you do with belts?

options.text: Inspect them only once a month.

questions.explanation: During your vehicle inspection, check all belts to make sure they are tight and not worn out.

questions.question: Before backing a vehicle where there are objects overhead, what should you do?

options.text: Cut any wires or branches in the way.
Get out and check the area before backing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and check the area before backing.
questions.explanation: You cannot see everything behind you when backing up. Before backing, get out and walk the path you will take. Look for anything that could hit your vehicle, especially objects overhead.

questions.question: What skill must you demonstrate on a basic vehicle control test?
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control test may include straight line backing, offset backing, parallel parking, and alley backing.

questions.question: Where are regrooved tires allowed on a bus?
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires are not allowed on the front of a bus.

questions.question: Where should a helper stand when backing a vehicle?

options.text: In front of the passenger's side.
In front of the driver's side.
Near the back of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the back of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: A helper should stand near the back of the vehicle where the driver can see them. They can watch the blind spots and help guide the driver safely.

questions.question: When should you check and adjust your mirrors?
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors before you start driving. Your posture may change, so your mirrors may need adjustment each day.

questions.question: What will you be asked to do during the vehicle inspection test?
questions.explanation: The vehicle inspection test includes checking the oil level. You must show it is within the safe operating range.

questions.question: What should you do when driving down a steep hill?

options.text: Shift to a low gear and use engine braking.
Downshift instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear and use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On long or steep downhill grades, use engine braking to control your speed. Use your brakes only to help with this.

questions.question: Strong winds usually cause the most problems for which vehicles?
questions.explanation: Strong winds make it hard to control your vehicle. This is usually a bigger problem for drivers of lighter commercial vehicles.

questions.question: What is important when loading a trailer?

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Put the right amount of weight over the axles.
Do not worry about how the weight is distributed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the right amount of weight over the axles.
questions.explanation: The weight on each axle must be balanced. Too little or too much weight can hurt steering, reduce traction, or damage the axles.

questions.question: What is black ice?

options.text: A thick layer of ice on the road.
A thin layer of ice on the road.
Ice that looks black because of road debris.

questions.correctAnswerText: A thin layer of ice on the road.
questions.explanation: Black ice is thin and clear enough that you can see the road through it. The road will look wet. Watch for black ice when the road looks wet but the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: How should you use a mirror?

options.text: Stare at it for a long time.
Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.explanation: Check mirrors with quick glances. If you spend too much time looking at a mirror, you will travel far without seeing what is ahead.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Make hand gestures at other drivers.
Assume other drivers have good reasons for their actions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers have good reasons for their actions.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, give other drivers the benefit of the doubt. Assume they have valid reasons for what they do. Don't take their actions personally.

questions.question: For a single vehicle with air brakes, the air leak rate should not exceed ____ in one minute during a static leakage test.
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test on a vehicle with air brakes, the leak rate should not exceed 2 psi in one minute. A faster leak rate means the brakes need repair before the vehicle can be driven.

questions.question: When inspecting your tires, which of these should you NOT find?

options.text: Tire tread that is 4/32 of an inch deep.

questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. Valve stems must not be cut or cracked. All tires should be the same size.

questions.question: Where is the tire load rating shown?

options.text: On the side of the tire.
On the inside of the tire.
On the inside of the driver's door.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of the tire.
questions.explanation: The tire load rating shows the maximum weight a tire can safely carry at a given pressure. This information is printed on the side of the tire.

questions.question: Is it safe to reach for a phone while driving?

options.text: Yes, if you are driving alone.
Yes, if you plan to use hands-free mode.
No, it is never safe, even with hands-free mode planned.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is never safe, even with hands-free mode planned.
questions.explanation: If you use a phone while driving, it must be within easy reach and positioned so you don't have to move unsafely. Reaching for a phone is dangerous and illegal, even if you plan to use hands-free features.

questions.question: When do you need an air brake endorsement?

options.text: To drive a vehicle with air brakes.
To drive any truck with a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: To drive a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: You must pass an air brakes knowledge test to be licensed to operate any vehicle with air brakes, including air over hydraulic systems.

questions.question: What is true about oversized loads?

options.text: They can never be transported by a truck.
They can only be transported during the day.
They need special permits to follow state and local laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need special permits to follow state and local laws.
questions.explanation: Special permits are required for loads that are oversized, over-length, or overweight.

questions.question: How long does it take for oil pressure to reach normal after starting an engine?
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should reach normal within seconds of starting the engine. Do not drive if oil pressure is low, dropping, or changing.

questions.question: What is blocking used for?

options.text: To put cargo in a large box.
To stop cargo from sliding in a trailer.
To stop cargo from falling out of a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: To stop cargo from sliding in a trailer.
questions.explanation: Blocking is placed on all sides of cargo to keep it from sliding when the vehicle moves.

questions.question: In cold weather, how often should you check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator?
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice buildup in the air brake system. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate allowed for a double combination vehicle during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: You need to know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle type. A double combination vehicle must not lose more than 4 psi of air pressure in one minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: How many driver licenses can one person have?

options.text: A regular license from one state and a CDL from another state.
Two licenses: one for cars and one for trucks.

questions.explanation: A person can only have one driver license. Having more than one license is illegal and can result in jail time and/or a fine up to $5,000.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a front brake limiting valve, where should you set it for normal stopping power?

options.text: Set it to the off position.

questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have front brake limiting valves with two settings: normal and slippery. The slippery setting reduces stopping power. Always set the valve to normal. Front wheel braking works well in all driving conditions.

questions.question: What information does NOT need to be included in an Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR)?
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include the trip dates and total distance traveled. It must also show fuel purchased. You do not need to record how many vehicles you passed.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most new heavy-duty trucks have?
questions.explanation: Most new heavy-duty trucks use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brake systems that share one set of brake controls.

questions.question: What will the examiner score you on during the driving test?

options.text: How fast you reach your destination.

questions.explanation: The examiner will score you on specific driving skills and overall driving behavior. You must drive safely, obey all traffic signs and signals, follow the law, and avoid accidents and moving violations.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: When stopped at a traffic signal

questions.explanation: Always check and adjust mirrors before you start each trip. The trailer should be straight when you adjust the mirrors.

questions.question: What should you do if your hydraulic brakes cannot build up enough pressure?

options.text: Push the brake pedal down as far as it will go.

questions.explanation: If your hydraulic brakes will not build enough pressure, try these steps: shift into a lower gear, pump the brakes, and/or use the emergency brake.

questions.question: What is required when operating a truck that needs a CDL?

options.text: You never have to wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if you carry more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if driving a tank vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: Every driver seat must have a seat belt. You must wear your seat belt at all times when driving a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: What does poor weight balance do to a vehicle?
questions.explanation: A poorly balanced load can cause unsafe handling. Always distribute cargo weight evenly when loading your vehicle.
